checks.rationale: Flat offline contracts own validation and digest only. The validator consumes the common implementation; installer changes remain within r4's bounded helper-closure allowance. No workflow or side-effect port implementation is added.

ADR-001 through ADR-005 remain honored: flat typed local artifacts, qualified identities, isolated exact candidate, separate higher-capability gates and preserved bounded recovery, plus unchanged project/managed ownership. Native submitted provenance limitations are explicit.

Accepted TASK-001 is in base ancestry and its source remains byte-identical. Six accepted TASK-003 DTO wire projections pass the new registry using immutable shared JSON. TASK-003 remains an independent sibling, without a new dependency or import.

Public flat imports reuse TASK-001 values and nonretryable domain errors. Five plan-local reference kinds retain constructor parity and reject missing/wrong qualification; project-unique plan references remain bare. No TASK-002 or TASK-039 implementation is consumed.

v1 schemas and bootstrap public symbol are unchanged. All 39 current tasks reproduce bootstrap and approved r4 digest bytes, including immutable inputs and task-order independence. The validator uses one recomputed digest with no stale fallback; registry errors remain strict and offline.

No schema migration occurs. Nested live records reject a conflicting plan owner; two plans can reuse local IDs. Physical plan relocation preserves five snapshot files exactly, including legacy JSON/original approval, while historical-byte tampering fails the snapshot-relative content hash.

The five changed paths exactly match task ownership. Flat modules, separate leaf tests, plan-local handoff, explicit namespaces and qualified-reference spelling follow existing conventions. No wrapper, centralized export or project-owned installation setting is changed.

No other task's service implementation is duplicated. The old ai.structural_task_digest symbol is intentionally retained as the r4/TASK-034 compatibility boundary; contracts owns the new common projection and the validator now uses it. Installer closure supports future wiring without implementing it.

Registry wire validation, common immutable values and service DTO ownership remain separate and compatible. Both mixed arrays use the documented closed whole-value language; unmatched prose remains structural. Explicit scope/reference fields retain declared semantics, without migration or filesystem-dependent inference.

R2 independently ran the declared 21 tests and integration probes for accepted DTOs, physical relocation/history, six actual stale-approval prose rejections and future transitive installed imports with a cycle. R1's 24 bootstrap tests, foundation, 54 relocations and offline boundary evidence were inspected without unnecessary broad repetition.

The owned handoff accurately describes signatures, recognition limits, exact bootstrap compatibility, transitive helper closure, evidence and retained failures. Documentation keeps later lifecycle/wiring work with its owners. Reports distinguish native submission from unavailable provider confirmation and disclose the corrected reviewer fixture.

Plan AC-01/REQ-01 and all TASK-004 criteria remain intact; approved r4 scope, dependencies and structural digest are unchanged. State/archive/CLI/release sequencing remains viable. Both failed R1 cycles and the single recovery allowance are preserved without budget reset, acceptance waiver or unaccepted dependency.
